author: Claude (English teacher role), authored against the v2 quality gate

slides.1: Every spring we wait for the rain, and nothing comes. Then the typhoons arrive and drop a whole year of water in two days. Today, let's watch our island cope.
slides.2: SDG 13 is Climate Action. Most people think it only means less carbon gas. It also means cities that survive a disaster, and water that still runs.
slides.3: Taiwan gets plenty of rain. But we are a water-poor island, because our mountains are steep. The rain runs into the sea before we can catch it.
slides.4: Typhoons now come less often, but they hit harder. In our worst drought, the reservoirs went dry. Rice fields cracked open, and the chip factories nearly stopped.
slides.5: Then the opposite happens. A year of rain can fall in two days. Our old drains cannot take it, so the streets turn into brown rivers.
slides.6: So here are the hard questions. Can our old pipes survive this new weather? And can we save the flood water for the dry months?
slides.7: Taiwan is already working on this. We now have the Forward-looking Water Grid. It joins the pipes of many cities, so Tainan can send spare water to Kaohsiung.
slides.8: Taipei and Taichung want to be sponge cities. New pavements let the rain soak through. Parks are built low, so a storm can fill them first.
slides.9: Our farmers are changing too. A computer gives each rice plant the exact water it needs, drop by drop. This saves millions of tons a year.
slides.10: How does STEM help? Engineers put small sensors inside the water pipes. The data goes to a computer, which finds a hidden leak in minutes.
slides.11: We also make new water. Factories clean their used water until it is pure again. On the coast, new plants take the salt out of sea water.
slides.12: Up in the mountains, we fight landslides too. Instead of tall cement walls, we use rocks and local plants. They hold the soil and keep our rivers clean.
slides.13: But none of this is cheap. New water plants and big pipes cost billions of dollars. So who pays for it? We must be fair to ordinary families.
slides.14: There is also a fair-share problem. The rich tech cities get the new water systems first. But small farm villages go dry first, and that is not right.
slides.15: Other islands have the same trouble, and our answers could help them. But Taiwan cannot speak at the big climate meetings. We must share in other ways.
slides.16: One more job is ours. We must check that these new systems still work, and are not just for show. Ask for the data every year.
slides.17: So what have we learned? Taiwan is learning to live with wild weather. Sponge cities, smart pipes and good engineering are making a weak island strong.
slides.18: Why does this matter to you? Because we still need better ideas. Study science, coding or engineering. And at home, save every drop you can.
slides.19: Please do not feel helpless. People are clever and nature is strong. Together they can protect this island and give our children a safe home.
slides.20: The weather will not wait for us. Will you help build a safer Taiwan? This island can be ready, and the work starts today.
